title: Define inline action protocol and hit target scaling for input affixes and clear/toggle controls
creator: Liam O'Neill
description: Background: Over the last six months we've received several dev and accessibility tickets about inconsistent hit targets, unpredictable keyboard focus flows, and visual collision between affix actions (clear, password reveal, inline toggles) and input validation indicators when density is compacted. This ticket defines a cross-platform protocol for inline actions (prefix/suffix icons that are actionable) and a tokenized approach for hitbox scaling so engineering can implement consistent behavior across TextField, Select, Multiline, and Password components. Goals: 1) Ensure minimum 44px interactive hit area for all inline actions at 'comfortable' density and scaled, predictable smaller targets at 'compact' density while preserving accessibility; 2) Establish keyboard and screen-reader behaviors for inline actions including focus order, aria-label patterns, and announcement expectations; 3) Define visual spacing tokens and motion for hover/focus/pressed states so validation icons and inline actions never overlap; 4) Provide detailed dev-ready specs, responsive rules, and QA checklist.
acceptance_criteria: All inline actions (clear, reveal, select dropdown triggers when styled as affix, toggle icons) have a documented minimum interactive area: 44px for comfortable and 36px for compact (measured center-to-edge), with token names tokens.hit.area.comfortable and tokens.hit.area.compact

Keyboard flow: tab order lands on input, subsequent Tab focuses first actionable affix (if present), Shift+Tab reverses; Enter/Space activates affix; aria-labels standardized as 'Clear input', 'Reveal password', 'Open options', or custom label from props

Validation state layering: validation icon uses layer token z.input.validation higher than affix icons; affix icons shift by tokens.spacing.affix-shift when validation icon present to maintain 8px minimum gap
Design tokens defined for spacing, hit area, icon sizes, and motion durations (tokens.icon.size.small|medium, tokens.hit.area.*, tokens.motion.short|medium)

Figma components updated: TextField (single-line), TextArea (multiline), Select (affix trigger variant), PasswordField have variants that demonstrate comfortable/compact/dense states with affix actions and validation states

Developer implementation checklist committed in a single GH issue linking to this ticket and the component PR, including accessibility tests (focus order, aria-label presence, screen reader announcement sample) and touch tests on iOS/Android emulators
Visual regression tests added showing overlap scenarios (icons + error badges) and confirmed no clipping at 320px viewport width
design_notes: Rationale: instead of ad-hoc padding hacks per component, use semantic hit-area tokens so designers and engineers compose reliably across density scales
Affix behavior: affix icon is visually centered in a hitbox that can extend into input padding; hitbox should be a separate focusable element to avoid input caret interference

Collision strategy: when validation/badge appears in suffix, affix shifts left by tokens.spacing.affix-shift; for constrained widths we show a condensed state where an overflow menu consolidates affixes - spec provided in Figma variant 'condensed-affixes'
Touch: mobile should favor comfortable hit area unless explicitly configured to compact; use CSS pointer-events and hitbox pseudo-elements to expand tappable region without changing visual size
Motion: focus/hover uses tokens.motion.short = 100ms for opacity and scale subtlety; pressed feedback is 50ms easing in/out

ARIA: affix buttons expose role='button' and aria-label; if affix action toggles state (e.g., reveal password), also include aria-pressed="false|true" and a live-region pattern for 'Password revealed' only when necessary for screen reader clarity

notes_for_engineers: Prefer separate button element for affixes instead of onclick handlers on svg to ensure consistent focusability across browsers
When expanding hit area with pseudo-element, use pointer-events: auto on the pseudo-element and pointer-events: none on the inner SVG to avoid double-handling
Provide an opt-out prop for legacy consumers who rely on previous padding (deprecated in next minor release)
Add visual regression targets in Percy for 320px, 375px, 768px widths showing affix+validation combinations
